notes: Access: direct HTTP fetch worked throughout (Shopify storefront, robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow, User-agent * Allow: /). Discovery: checked main nav/header, homepage featured sections, footer, /pages/sitemap nav page, and a full /collections.json sweep (95 collections) for Bestsellers-type terms. Found 4 candidate collections, none linked from main nav/header/homepage/sitemap page (all discoverable only via the /collections.json sweep): best-sellers (title 'Best Sellers'), best-selling-decor ('Best Selling Decor'), best-selling-furniture ('Best Selling Furnitures'), best-selling-lamps ('Best Selling Lamps'). Each opened and confirmed as a real product grid (not editorial/PDP). collections.json 'products_count' is known-inflated on this store (prior Home-Decor pass finding); used each collection page's own embedded 'product_count' JSON field plus an independent exhaustive /collections/<handle>/products.json id-enumeration, which agreed exactly in all 4 cases (246, 9, 9, 34). The 3 sub-collections (9+9+34=52) do not sum to the 246 total, and none of the 4 pages cross-link to the others or breadcrumb as parent/child, so they are recorded as flat sibling listings of the same Bestsellers concept rather than a formal group+children structure. Flagged the 3 sub-collections for manual review solely because they are non-navigable orphans (only found via the raw JSON sweep) -- the qty figures themselves are exact and verified. Site's own homepage hero also has a '/collections/all?sort_by=best-selling' sort-order link; that is a sort parameter on the full catalog, not a genuine Bestsellers PLP, and was excluded. No other bestseller/popular/trending/customer-favorite named collection exists anywhere in the 95-collection sweep.
